title: The looks of one component stay together as a set
goal: When a button has a resting, hovered, pressed and disabled look, the four drawings should sit together on the page so you can see them as one set. Today the app drops each new one wherever it finds room, so on a page that is not wide enough you get one drawing on its own with its copies underneath and the other three stacked in a column beside it, and nothing says the four belong together.
notes:
Reproduced on 2026-09-23 with Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/tutorial-component-versions-walk.json --no-build. The guide builds all four states on its own sample page (720x480, button 240x52 starting at 88,88) and its last step promises "Four drawings under one name, each labelled with its state". The render it leaves, /tmp/photonz-playtest/tutorial-component-versions-walk/7-four-states-built-doc.png, is Default at top left with its two copies below it and Hover, Pressed and Disabled in a column to its right.

Why: PhotonzDocument.roomForDrawing (Sources/PhotonzCore/ComponentVersions.swift) is a generic packer. It walks along the row the SOURCE drawing is on, steps over anything in the way, and when the row runs out of canvas it drops to a fresh row under the blockers. Four 240-wide drawings with the 24pt gap need 1032pt and the sample page is 720, so the third and fourth wrap. On a 1440 wide page they do land in a row, which is why the journey walk (Scripts/playtest/button-states-journey-walk.json) looks right and the tutorial does not.

This was measured twice before: make-a-button-with-states-and-properties-and-set logged it on 2026-09-15 and tutorials-making-states-in-a-component folded it on 2026-09-16. Both left it because the fix is a real decision rather than a tweak: keeping a set together on a page too narrow for it means either wrapping them deliberately into a grid of the component's own, growing the page, or giving the component a strip that holds its looks. That decision is the first act of this task.
acceptance: Adding a look to a component puts it with the looks that component already has, not wherever there happens to be room
Four looks of one component read as one set on a page too narrow to lay them out in a single row
The states tutorial, on its own sample page, ends with the four drawings together rather than one plus a column
A picture in the audit shows the four looks of a button as a set

log.note: Reproduced with Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/tutorial-component-versions-walk.json: render 7 showed Default alone, its two copies under it, and Hover/Pressed/Disabled in a column at x=352.

Root cause is wider than the notes said: addComponentVersion searched for room from the SOURCE look, so adding each state from the one just made produced the column even on an empty 720 page (new ComponentVersionRoomTests.looksAddedOneFromTheNextFormOneGridWithTheFirst failed with [(88,88),(352,88),(352,164),(352,240)]). The copies under the original were a second cause in the guide.

Decision taken (no card): the looks wrap into rows of their own, read from the component's FIRST look. Least invasive of the three in the notes, never changes the page size, and is what any later outlined-set box would lay out inside. Growing the page was ruled out as changing the document under the person. The outlined set (Figma style) is raised as an evaluate question on the audit instead of a card, so the user's reaction files it if wanted.

Shipped: ComponentVersions.addComponentVersion anchors roomForDrawing on the first look's canvas box. Shared component placement already anchored on the first look. Starter drop placement untouched. Guide sample copies moved from y=192/296 to y=264/368 so the set's second row is free; both guide walks' copy click moved to (176,290).

Verified: 3 new room tests + tutorial test asserting two rows of two; Scripts/test.sh 11035 passed; 11 walks that add looks all ok (tutorial-component-versions, tutorial-override-one-copy, button-states-journey, component-versions, apply-to-versions, place-a-version, version-*, name-chip-reads-anywhere, dock-component-first, component-whole-path). Real capture 10-all-four-together-sc.png shows the 2x2 set.

Left rough (audit rough, not filed): no outline marks the set as one thing; something parked where the set's next row goes still breaks it up in a person's own document; state labels sit tight in the 24pt row gap. All three are on the audit for the user to react to; none is broken, and 'a version set drawn as one thing' was already named as not-in-slice in ui-building.md.

New looks of a component land with the set, read from its first look, so four states on a narrow page are two rows of two (ComponentVersions.addComponentVersion). States guide sample copies moved below the set. Verified: new room + tutorial tests, full suite 11035 passed, 11 look-adding walks ok, real capture in audit 2026-10-03-component-looks-set.
